headline: Moon Explorers Begin New Chapter Mentoring NASA's Future
meta_description: Victor Glover and Reid Wiseman, who flew farther than anyone before on Artemis II, transition to emeritus roles to mentor NASA teams preparing for lunar missio…
summary_short: Two pioneering astronauts who orbited the Moon are now guiding the next generation of space explorers through NASA's emeritus program.
body:
Victor Glover and Reid Wiseman, who became the first humans in over 50 years to reach lunar orbit aboard Artemis II earlier this year, are stepping into a new role at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston. Both astronauts are transitioning to emeritus status in September, a position that allows experienced personnel to volunteer their expertise while maintaining flexibility for outside opportunities. Rather than ending their NASA careers, the move marks a shift toward mentoring and advising the teams preparing for Artemis III in 2027 and beyond. Their knowledge of Orion spacecraft systems and deep-space operations will prove invaluable as the agency accelerates preparations for returning astronauts to the lunar surface.

Wiseman commanded Artemis II after spending 165 days aboard the International Space Station, while Glover contributed his experience as a naval aviator and test pilot. Together with NASA astronaut Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen, the pair completed a historic 10-day mission that saw them travel farther into space than anyone before. "There is no better place to work, and there are no better people to work with, than those in this agency," Wiseman said of his decision to remain involved through the emeritus program.

NASA leadership emphasized that this transition represents not a farewell, but a continuation of service. Scott Tingle, chief of the Astronaut Office, called the pair "trusted teammates whose professionalism, calm leadership, and unwavering commitment to NASA have strengthened our office." Glover plans to remain engaged in aerospace, leadership, and public service both within NASA and beyond, while helping younger astronauts and engineers reach toward humanity's next giant leap.
quick_facts: Artemis II crew became first humans in 50+ years to reach lunar orbit
Wiseman previously spent 165 days aboard the International Space Station
Glover and Wiseman transitioned to emeritus status at Johnson Space Center
Artemis III lunar mission planned for 2027
